title: Detour

evidence.note: Searched the Catalog of Copyright Entries motion-picture volumes for 1972 (catalogofc19723261213libr), 1973 (catalogofc19733271213libr) and 1974 (catalogofcopyrig3281213li) and found no Detour renewal. The check was a read-through of the volume text by a summarizing tool, not a literal string search, so it is not conclusive. One apparent 1974 hit, R587019, turned out to be 'Dark passage'. The original 1945 registration entry was not located. Non-renewal is therefore not proven here.
Companion renewal volume for 1974, read the same way, with no Detour entry found.
Companion renewal volume for 1972, read the same way, with no Detour entry found.
Wikipedia credits Leo Erdody with the original score. Detour is a sound film, so the recorded track would normally share the print's status. No separate music registration or renewal was checked.
The screenplay adapts Martin M. Goldsmith's 1939 novel of the same title. Whether the novel's copyright was renewed could not be confirmed, so the source's status is unknown.

The Film Foundation describes a restoration by the Academy Film Archive and The Film Foundation, using a MoMA 35mm duplicate negative, a Brussels nitrate print and a Cinémathèque Française print. Roundabout Entertainment removed the French and Flemish subtitles from the Brussels print and filled missing frames. This looks like a faithful restoration with no added score or titles, so it should add no new US copyright. That is not confirmed for every release of it.

editorial:
Detour is a 1945 film noir directed by Edgar G. Ulmer for the Poverty Row studio Producers Releasing Corporation, with a score by Leo Erdody. It had a Boston premiere on November 15, 1945, and was selected for the National Film Registry in 1992. The film adapts Martin M. Goldsmith's 1939 novel. Reusers like it for its cheap, tight noir look, and several copies circulate on the Internet Archive.

The rights trap is that the film's public-domain status is widely repeated but not confirmed here. A read-through of the 1972, 1973 and 1974 renewal volumes found no Detour entry, but the method was not a literal search and the 1945 registration was not located. The 1939 novel is a separate work with its own renewal history, which was not checked. The Academy Film Archive and Film Foundation restoration removed subtitles from a Belgian print and filled missing frames. That appears faithful, but check what any specific restored release adds before reusing it.
faq: Can I upload the Internet Archive copy of Detour to my own channel?

The Internet Archive tags its copies as public domain, but this review did not prove that no renewal exists. A read-through of the 1972 to 1974 renewal volumes found nothing, which is suggestive, not conclusive. Run your own search of the Copyright Office and renewal records first. Do not assume a restored release is free to reuse.
Does the 1939 novel affect my use of the film?
It can. The film adapts Goldsmith's novel, which is a separate work with its own renewal history. This review could not confirm whether the novel's renewal was filed.
